rv.q: Happily, that risk has paid off and Cursed Child hasn’t lost any of its sparkle.

Jack Thorne’s spellbinding theatrical sequel to Harry Potter – with JK Rowling’s creative involvement – has marked its 10th anniversary in the West End by downsizing from two parts to one, the running-time slashed from five hours to three.

Thorne and the director John Tiffany have come up with an enjoyably brisk, if occasionally opaque piece of story-telling in which the magic tricks and illusions catch the eye even when the plot twists whizz past like broomsticks caught in a hurricane.
Overall, this is an exciting production that will bring plenty of joy to fans.
The blending of the everyday world with the supernatural and surreal world of Hogwarts is simply ingenious.

cn.t: Critics praise this streamlined one-part adaptation as spellbinding and richly absorbing, with its magic and superb performances fully intact despite the condensed three-hour runtime.

sg.ra: Choose Center Orchestra Rows D-M for the best views of the stage.
Choose center orchestra rows N-W for a great view without paying a hefty price.
Choose Center Mezzanine Rows A-D for the best views of the stage.
Avoid these seats if you want a clear view of the stage.

vs.sum: Spectacularly renovated in a $100M+ project that literally raised the theater 30 feet. The restoration preserved its opulent 1913 interior while upgrading acoustics, seating comfort, and best-in-class restrooms on every level — widely considered the best facilities on Broadway.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Wheelchair, aisle transfer, and companion seating on all levels.
